symptom: A pluggable widget mxcli writes fails **CE0463** even with no action and nothing but `Attribute:` set, while the SAME widget placed by hand in Studio Pro in the same project is clean. Slider and RangeSlider both
cause: **Two causes, and neither alone is enough.** (A) The bare `Attribute:` keyword filled EVERY attribute-typed mapping — a Slider declares four (`valueAttribute`, `min/max/stepAttribute`), so one keyword wrote the same AttributeRef into all of them, and Studio Pro leaves min/max/step unset unless the matching `*ValueType` is "attribute". (B) `tooltip` got a populated `Forms$ClientTemplate` where Studio Pro stores `TextTemplate: nil` — the #574 class — because the visibility extractor lifted only the ELSE branch of `showTooltip ? "value"===tooltipType && hide("tooltip") : hide(["tooltip",…])`, so a tooltip hidden by the widget's own DEFAULTS read as visible and `ApplyVisibilityRules` took its *visible* branch and FILLED an empty template
insight: **Diff the two widgets in ONE project file, and diff the `Type` first to eliminate it**: here the whole `Type` — 27 PropertyTypes, their order, their nested ValueType maps, the metadata — was **byte-equivalent** once random `$ID`s were normalised, which rules out schema/order/template-version and leaves only the stored `Object`. **A conjunction is not expressible** as one `WidgetVisibilityCondition`, so the then-branch's inner condition is emitted ONLY when another rule hides the same property under the negation of the outer one — the else branch — making the pair a correct disjunction (`hidden ⟺ ¬showTooltip ∨ tooltipType=="value"`); without that cover, skipping is safe (degrades to "not hidden") and guessing is CE0463's mirror image. **Why Slider and not ProgressCircle**, whose shape looks identical: ProgressCircle parenthesises the branch, which the existing grouping-paren strip removes; Slider does not, so the guard arrived as `e.showTooltip?"value"===e.tooltipType` and `lastGuardExpr` handed back a `?` boundary nothing handled. **A hidden list can be COMPUTED and then nothing is liftable** — Slider's min/max/step hides are `[].concat(n(v[e.minValueType]), …)`, table lookups with no string literal — so the hidden-property guard cannot cover cause A at all; not writing the property is the only fix that does not depend on that data. Issue #238
